claim_being_audited: That certifying the current model release is policy-compliant because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and the material housing voucher recertification weakness can be handled through disclosure/context rather than blocking certification.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if the current release documentation reflects current evaluation results.
Certification is compliant only if the material segment weakness is explicitly disclosed or covered by approved mitigation/risk acceptance.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring notes may provide context but cannot substitute for current release-specific evidence.
Public governance guidance can support framing, but cannot replace required internal policy predicates for certification.
evidence_requests: Provide the current release documentation or model card text showing the current evaluation results and explicit disclosure of the housing voucher recertification weakness.
Provide any approved mitigation, reviewed risk acceptance, or owner sign-off covering this material segment weakness before launch.
Provide the governing materiality determination or launch-use-case mapping showing why this segment weakness is or is not material for certification.
specific_concerns: The policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and disclose material segment weaknesses or show approved mitigation; the summary does not establish that this documentation update actually exists.
The packet itself states the release thread contains only an informal monitoring comment and lacks reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language.
Prior approval is explicitly only contextual because it predates the current retrieval change and current evaluation batch.
Public Hugging Face and NIST materials may support governance principles, but they do not independently satisfy the release policy predicate for this specific certification decision.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant, rather than only potentially supportable if the model card/release record is updated with the current regression disclosure.
Any implication that informal post-launch monitoring constitutes approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance.
Any implication that prior approval of the model family materially closes the gap created by the current release-specific regression.
